thread:
Maya P: quick brain-dump — can we sketch a tiny contract for a format-agnostic loader that lets runtime do 'weight contraction' (fusion + quant decompression) as a pluggable step? thinking about cold-start cost and long-term maintainability. :thinking:
Kevin L: short answer: yes, but we need strong guarantees on ordering and backpressure. otherwise you'll end up with weird races during prefix warmup.
Olga R: can you outline the invariants you want? e.g., does contraction mutate bytes on-disk or only produce ephemeral in-memory slices?
Maya P: ephemeral only. idea is to keep original shard blobs immutable. loader exposes a stream + metadata and a small sidecar API so the runtime can request an on-the-fly transformed slice. benefits: cheaper rollbacks, easier provenance. downsides: slightly more CPU at load time.
Samir J: important: the contract must include a checksum + size for each transformed chunk so fallback (if contraction fails) can fetch raw bytes and fall back to runtime-side transformation. otherwise rollouts are unsafe.
Theo B: +1 to checksum. also we should include a 'priority_hint' per chunk for warmup scheduler. some heads are more latency-sensitive. e.g., attention kv vs embedding table.
Maya P: exactly. sketch of a minimal loader API (pseudo-Python):
```python
class WeightSliceDesc(NamedTuple):
    offset: int
    length: int
    content_type: str  # "raw", "quantized", "contracted"
    checksum: str
    priority_hint: int

class Loader:
    def manifest(path) -> List[WeightSliceDesc]
    def stream_slice(slice_desc) -> AsyncIterator[bytes]
    def request_contract(slice_desc, contract_spec) -> ContractReceipt
```
ContractReceipt contains transformed checksum + size + optional latency_estimate.
Kevin L: that looks ok. need to add explicit 'lease' (timebound) so warmup can prefetch without holding permanent ownership of memory. otherwise we leak caches.
Maya P: fair. proposal: request_contract returns receipt with lease_ms and 'evictable' boolean. runtime can renew lease or release early.
Olga R: how do we handle multi-shard slices that cross file boundaries? e.g., micro-shard layout that packs tensors across objects. 
Samir J: loader should expose atomic 'composite slice' descriptors and an inexpensive assemble path. but the contract semantics must still guarantee idempotence so second contract attempt yields same checksum.
Theo B: we also need a graceful fallback path for memory-constrained nodes: provide an index-first path where the manifest yields fully-resolvable byte-ranges and the runtime can do a smaller, streaming decode without materializing full contracted buffer. something like 'stream_decoder' that yields kv frames.
Maya P: yes — two orthogonal paths: 1) contract-on-demand (fast, may allocate temp buffers) 2) index-first streaming (low mem, slightly slower). Both share same descriptors/checksums so verification is uniform.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary loader-proxy v0.4 was rolled to staging at 2026-02-12 18:12 UTC :rocket:
Kevin L: operational note — any contract needs an observable trace: latency, cpu, mem, transform-fail-rate. otherwise Optimize can't make recommendations. add tags: model, shard-id, slice-id, contract-spec.
Olga R: implementation concern: how do we version contract_spec? we need a tiny semantic version in receipts so older runtimes can detect incompatible transforms. e.g., quant->fp16 contract v2 vs v3 behavior differences.
Samir J: agreed. contract_spec should include a short id + human string + compatible_versions list. receipts include used_version.
Maya P: tradeoffs recap I posted to #eng-ml RFC earlier but TL;DR: pros — immutable originals, safe rollbacks, cheaper ops to mutate in-memory; cons — more complex loader boundary and slightly more runtime coupling to contract semantics.
Theo B: my practical ask: add 'priority_hint' semantics to WarmupScheduler: 0=background, 1=high, 2=critical. warmup should age-based demote hints if budget exceeded.
Kevin L: also add 'budget_token' bookkeeping to loader so system can throttle on-disk decompress. e.g., each contract consumes X tokens proportional to bytes_transformed. that lets us cap global CPU for contraction work.
Maya P: agreed. we should prototype on a single-model e2e: use a small Llama7b-style checkpoint, implement two contract_specs (quant-decompress, fuse-linear). measure cold-start p95 with and without contract caching.
Olga R: I'll help write the manifest schema and a small test harness that can verify idempotence and checksum equality.
Samir J: I'll wire telemetry into loader-proxy to emit transform-fail events + latency histograms.
Theo B: I'll update WarmupScheduler to support priority_hint and budget_token accounting.
Maya P: thanks team. next steps: prototype branch + small doc PR that lists the contract fields and example receipts. aiming for a short RFC follow-up next week.
Kevin L: minor: add note to docs that loaders must never mutate source shards in-place. that rule will save headaches. :exclamation:
Maya P: noted. will add.
infra-bot: incident-bot: low-memory alert triggered on staging-rt-07 at 3178901375 — sample trace shows large contracted buffers during simultaneous warmup. tagging @Theo B
Theo B: saw it — will ensure evictable=true default for staging to avoid OOM spikes until we have caching caps.
Maya P: ok wrapping up. leaving a short checklist in this thread for the PR: [manifest schema, contract_spec versioning, lease semantics, checksum verification tests, telemetry events].
Olga R: added to my todo.
Samir J: ping me when harness ready, I can run nightly.
Maya P: thanks all :thumbsup:
